title: Two-tail specificity test: pre-registration for the revision
status: DRAFT until scripts/freeze_prereg.py has written two_tail_prereg.lock.json and both files are committed. Edit only before freezing.
supersedes_note: Extends the original pre-specification (commit 2bcfd96). Nothing frozen there is changed; this file adds the new concepts, the window-size sweep, the multiplicity rule and the equivalence bound.
gemma_policy: Every test is reported twice, with all eight models and without gemma-2-2b. gemma-2-2b failed the split-half reliability gate on the concept side (section 4.3), so the without-gemma result is the one consistent with that rule; the with-gemma result is reported so that no conclusion rests on the exclusion. A conclusion is stated as robust only if it holds in both.
unit_of_analysis: model. Concepts are averaged within a model before testing, because concepts in one model share an eigenbasis and are not independent.
basis_note: Primary tests use the published language-subset basis (en-fr/cov_src.pt) so both tails are measured in the basis the published claims were made in. The full-vocabulary basis is a pre-specified robustness check, run into its own folder.

loud_tail.claim_tested: the high-variance head carries syntax specifically
loud_tail.label: UD English-EWT part of speech, 500 sentences, published filter
loud_tail.k_frac_note: 0.10 is the published window size; it is primary because the published claim was made at it.

quiet_tail.claim_tested: the low-variance tail carries concepts specifically
quiet_tail.k_frac_note: 0.005 is the window size the original concept-side runs used. It is frozen here BEFORE the new concepts are run.

exclusion_rule.floor_check: drop a cell whose shuffled-label probe is more than 0.05 from the majority rate

k_sweep_role: Robustness only. The sweep is reported in full for both tails and both layers; no conclusion is drawn from a k other than the primary one, and no k is promoted after the fact.

inference.test: one-sample t-test over models (two-sided), Wilcoxon signed-rank reported alongside
inference.primary_rule: One primary test per tail (above). Each primary is tested at alpha = 0.05; the two primaries address different claims.

family.missing_member_rule: A family member that was not run enters Holm with p = 1, so the family size stays 8 and the correction is never weakened by omission.

quantities.delta: specificity: retention gap of the real label minus that of the control
quantities.gap: tilt: retention gap of the real label alone (loud: top minus bottom; quiet: bottom minus top)

equivalence.applies_to: every quiet-tail family member; reported for the loud tail as well
equivalence.scale: retention units (fraction of the label's own full-dimensional signal)
equivalence.rationale: A window that retains ten percentage points more of a concept's own decodable signal than the control does is the smallest difference we would describe as the tail 'holding' the concept. It equals the concept-headroom threshold already used to exclude cells. Set before the new concepts were run; not chosen from the data.
equivalence.non_superiority: Specificity is a directional claim, so a one-sided test of H0: mean delta >= +sesoi is also reported for both tails.

length_control.diagnostic: For every dataset report the AUC of character length (and token count) for the concept label, and the share of pairs whose positive member is longer.
length_control.balance: subsample pairs so the positive member is longer exactly as often as the negative
length_control.residualise: regress [chars, log chars, words, tokens] out of the activations the concept probe sees
length_control.reading: If the quiet-tail delta stays inside the equivalence bound under both, the length-control objection does not change the conclusion.

nonlinear_probe.probe: one hidden layer, 256 units, ReLU, dropout 0.1, AdamW, early stopping on a 10% split of the training fold
nonlinear_probe.role: robustness; reported with the same primary k, layer and controls
